score_notes.novelty: The uncatalogued pairing of Hepworth’s pierced form with CSS shape-outside text exclusion creates a genuinely web-only negative-space sculpture, though it does not open an entirely new artistic ontology.
score_notes.nuance: The exclusion mechanism and sculpture argument are one object, but the long prose explicitly explains the invisible-hole gag and therefore spends the restrained second reading it otherwise earns.
score_notes.narrative: It materially restages Hepworth’s named 1931 sculpture, but the claimed chance side is only deterministic device-dependent reflow rather than a legible chance mechanism.
score_notes.craft: The dependency-free shape-outside implementation, single control, and absence of fallbacks or unused machinery make this close to the smallest build that completes the thought.
score_notes.wit: The retreating prose and ‘carve’ control land as a clean conceptual gag once, while the earnest explanation largely prevents a dry second laugh.

references_named: Henry Moore, the hole as positive form
rationale: All hard gates pass: the work is web-native, makes a clear argument about sculptural absence, and enacts that argument through live CSS text exclusion rather than merely illustrating it. It is materially distinct from the catalogue’s clip-path, visibility, and source-versus-render works, while its compact no-network implementation satisfies the open-license and attribution requirements. Its main weakness is that the lengthy explanatory prose names the art-historical answer and browser trick explicitly, while the claimed chance axis is overstated.
reservations: The didactic paragraph both supplies the art-historical reading and explains the browser trick, weakening P7; P5 is also overstated because resize-dependent wrapping is contingency rather than genuine chance.
revision_suggestion: Shorten and de-explain the running prose while retaining enough text to reveal the bend, then either introduce a real per-visit chance variable or remove the chance claim; keep the implementation otherwise.
